findings.evidence: lock a Member account after 5 consecutive failed login attempts within a 10-minute window
findings.rationale: Does not specify the lockout duration, the unlock condition or recovery mechanism (automatic timeout vs. administrative unlock), or the error response returned to the locked-out Member.

findings.evidence: notify him by email
findings.rationale: The pronoun 'him' has an ambiguous antecedent and could refer to the Librarian, the Member, or the Guarantor.

findings.evidence: TBD minutes
findings.rationale: Contains an unresolved 'TBD' placeholder instead of a concrete token expiration duration.

findings.evidence: user-friendly; easy to navigate; loads rapidly; standard connections
findings.rationale: Uses subjective, unquantified terms without measurable usability criteria, load-time thresholds, or network bandwidth definitions.

findings.evidence: TBD consecutive times
findings.rationale: Contains an unresolved 'TBD' placeholder instead of specifying the maximum number of consecutive loan renewals.

findings.evidence: validate item eligibility within 2 seconds and issue the loan receipt
findings.rationale: Specifies only the successful checkout path and omits error handling for ineligible items, invalid or unreadable barcodes, or validation failures.

findings.evidence: the allowed maximum number of active hold requests
findings.rationale: References an allowed maximum number of active hold requests without defining the actual numeric limit.

findings.evidence: borrow up to 8 physical items simultaneously
findings.rationale: Allows a Member in good standing to borrow up to 8 physical items simultaneously, contradicting SD-009 which caps simultaneous checkouts at 5 physical items.

findings.evidence: 21 calendar days from the checkout timestamp
findings.rationale: Sets the standard loan period for circulating print books to 21 calendar days, contradicting SD-010 which sets it to 14 calendar days.

findings.evidence: self-register online with only an email address and immediately check out physical books without Librarian ID verification
findings.rationale: Permits unverified visitors to self-register with only an email address and check out books without ID verification, contradicting SD-001 which requires a Librarian to verify government-issued photo ID and record full name, email, and phone number.

findings.evidence: remain held indefinitely until the requesting Member explicitly cancels the hold
findings.rationale: States that reserved items on the pickup shelf are held indefinitely until explicitly cancelled by the Member, contradicting SD-011 which requires automatic cancellation after exactly 72 hours.

findings.evidence: send an overdue email and/or suspend borrowing privileges and/or apply a penalty flag
findings.rationale: Uses chained 'and/or' conjunctions without specifying which exact combination of the three actions must be executed or under what conditions each applies.

findings.evidence: shall be reviewed, approved, and recorded
findings.rationale: Uses passive voice without identifying which actor or role (e.g., Librarian, Administrator, Billing Service) is responsible for reviewing, approving, and recording fine waiver requests; it also omits handling for rejections or requests above $25.00 USD.

findings.evidence: before the due date if appropriate
findings.rationale: The weak phrase 'if appropriate' leaves the condition for dispatching SMS alerts subjective and untestable, and 'before the due date' does not specify a concrete lead time.

findings.evidence: TBD years
findings.rationale: Contains an unresolved 'TBD' placeholder instead of a defined retention period for payment receipts.

findings.evidence: $1.25 USD per overdue day per item with no maximum cap
findings.rationale: Sets the overdue fine to $1.25 USD per day with no cap, contradicting SD-019 which sets the fine to $0.50 USD per day capped at $20.00 USD per item.

findings.evidence: renew borrowed items online at any time regardless of any unpaid overdue fine balance
findings.rationale: Allows Members to renew borrowed items regardless of unpaid overdue fines, contradicting SD-020 which blocks renewals when unpaid fines exceed $5.00 USD.

findings.evidence: Patron's active loan count and enforce the 5-item borrowing limit on the Patron profile screen
findings.rationale: Introduces the inconsistent term 'Patron' instead of 'Member' used across the SRS (e.g., SD-009) for the same borrowing entity, and also reasserts a 5-item borrowing limit that conflicts with SD-015's 8-item limit.

findings.evidence: quickly; many users
findings.rationale: Uses unquantified vague terms ('quickly', 'many users') without specifying maximum response latency or concurrent user load targets.

findings.evidence: where possible
findings.rationale: The weak phrase 'where possible' makes term highlighting subjective and untestable by failing to define when highlighting is mandatory versus omitted.

findings.evidence: sufficient ISBN matching accuracy; acceptable response times
findings.rationale: Uses subjective vague terms ('sufficient', 'acceptable') without quantifiable accuracy metrics or maximum response-time bounds.

findings.evidence: efficiently; large batch MARC21 files; without noticeable system slowdown
findings.rationale: Uses vague, unmeasurable terms without defining throughput targets, batch size limits, or acceptable system latency degradation.

findings.evidence: shall detect the active references
findings.rationale: States only that the Catalog Service must detect active loans or holds on deletion attempts, omitting the required resulting action (e.g., blocking deletion and returning an error).

findings.evidence: TBD intervals
findings.rationale: Contains an unresolved 'TBD' placeholder instead of a defined backup schedule interval.

findings.evidence: important administrative actions; in a timely manner; appropriate period
findings.rationale: Uses vague, unquantified terms that leave which administrative events must be logged, the maximum logging latency, and the retention period undefined.

findings.evidence: the Failover Manager shall log event FAILOVER-01
findings.rationale: Specifies only logging FAILOVER-01 when the primary database node becomes unreachable for over 10 seconds, omitting the actual failover and recovery actions (such as promoting a standby node, rerouting traffic, or alerting Administrators).

findings.evidence: adequate transport security; clear error messages
findings.rationale: Uses subjective vague terms without specifying concrete transport security standards (e.g., TLS version and cipher suites) or verifiable criteria for authentication error messages.

findings.evidence: accept any Member password of at least 8 characters
findings.rationale: Accepts any password of at least 8 characters, contradicting SD-002 which requires at least 12 characters containing uppercase, lowercase, and numeric characters.

findings.evidence: 60 minutes of user inactivity
findings.rationale: Keeps web portal sessions active for 60 minutes of inactivity, contradicting SD-004 which terminates sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity.

findings.evidence: reversible AES-256 encryption so Administrators can decrypt and retrieve forgotten passwords
findings.rationale: Mandates reversible AES-256 encryption so passwords can be decrypted and retrieved, directly contradicting SD-003 which mandates one-way bcrypt hashing and prohibits storing or exposing plaintext passwords.
